messages.content: My lord, a cesarean section—commonly called a C‑section—is a surgical operation in which a baby is delivered through an incision made in the mother’s abdomen and uterus. The procedure is performed when a vaginal delivery would pose significant risk to either the mother or the child, such as in cases of fetal distress, abnormal positioning of the fetus, placental complications, or maternal health concerns. The surgeon opens the abdominal wall, then carefully enters the uterine cavity to remove the baby before closing the incisions. It is a common, well‑established method for ensuring safe delivery when circumstances warrant it.

My lord, a cesarean section—often called a C‑section—is the surgical delivery of a baby through an incision made in the mother’s abdomen and uterus. The operation is undertaken when a vaginal birth would present undue danger to either the mother or the child, such as fetal distress, malposition of the fetus, placental complications, or maternal health concerns. The surgeon opens the abdominal wall, enters the uterine cavity, removes the infant, and then closes both incisions. It is a common, well‑established procedure used to ensure the safety of mother and child when circumstances warrant it.
